overview.title: 📖 Overview: Deriving the Rules of Separate Tithing
overview.subtitle: Bekhorot 54a–54b
overview.hebrewSource: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה מִצְטָרֵף כִּמְלֹא רֶגֶל בְּהֵמָה רוֹעָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf continues building, through a chain of a fortiori inferences, the principle that different species or categories of produce and animals cannot be tithed for one another — wine cannot cover grain, cattle cannot cover flock, and old-year animals cannot cover new-year ones. Rava eventually retracts an earlier position and settles the matter through the verse's own juxtapositions. The daf then turns to a new mishna: animals scattered across a distance join together for tithing purposes only within the reach of a single shepherd's eye — sixteen mil — and the Gemara works out, through Rav and Shmuel's dispute, exactly how many animals in the middle bridge a wider gap.

slides.title: 🍇 Building the Chain: No Species Tithes Another
slides.subtitle: From wine-and-oil to grain-and-grain by a fortiori reasoning

steps.content: 1️⃣ Established: wine and oil cannot be tithed for each other (from 'give the best of this, and of that')
2️⃣ A fortiori: if wine/oil — not even subject to diverse-kinds — still can't combine, surely wine/grain or grain/grain, which ARE diverse kinds, cannot combine either

3️⃣ Rabbi Yoshiya's harder case: he requires a single-handed sowing of wheat, barley, AND grape seed together for the diverse-kinds prohibition to apply at all — so the simple a fortiori doesn't work for him

4️⃣ His alternative: wine/oil aren't diverse kinds EVEN WITH added seeds; grain pairs ARE diverse kinds when combined with something else — so the a fortiori still holds, just via a different comparison

slides.title: 🐐 Cattle vs. Flock, and Sheep vs. Goats
slides.subtitle: Abaye and Rava dispute the textual source

lines.speaker: Question
lines.text: The verse doesn't say 'tithe of cattle AND tithe of flock' twice — so why can't they be tithed together, the way sheep and goats can?

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: 'The TENTH shall be sacred' — give the tenth from THIS one, and the tenth from THAT one, separately. Sheep and goats combine only because 'or flock' groups them as one category.

lines.speaker: Rava (first view)
lines.text: No verse is even needed — animal tithe is juxtaposed to grain tithe: just as different grains don't combine, different animal species don't combine either.

lines.speaker: Rava (retracted)
lines.text: I later retracted that — the juxtaposition to grain tithe was only about NEW vs. OLD flocks ('year by year'), not about species in general. (Some attribute this retraction to Rav Pappa instead.)

slides.title: 🔁 Two Explanations for the Same Verse
slides.subtitle: Why 'flock' includes sheep and goats but not cattle
rows: Rav Huna b. Rav Naḥman's challenge
Suggests 'herd or flock' means intermingle them all!
Answered: Rava already accepts Abaye's 'the tenth' derivation, ruling this out
Grain tithe juxtaposition itself bars mixing any two types
Same juxtaposition — extends even to herd vs. flock, without needing 'the tenth'

slides.title: 🚶 How Far Can a Shepherd's Flock Spread?
slides.subtitle: The new mishna's sixteen-mil rule

nodes.content: 📜 Mishna: animals join for tithing within the span a single shepherd can walk and still tend them — 16 mil
📖 Source: Jeremiah 33:12–13, 'the flock shall again pass under the hands of him who counts them' — one shepherd's flock is one unit
👁️ Tradition: a shepherd's eye reaches sixteen mil — that becomes the halakhic maximum distance
❌ Beyond 32 mil total (16+16), the two groups do NOT combine at all

slides.title: 🌉 Bridging the Gap: Rav vs. Shmuel
slides.subtitle: How many animals in the middle unite two distant flocks?

boxes.title: Rav's View
items: Five animals on each end plus five in the middle
The middle five can combine with either side to reach ten
That connects both distant flocks into one unit

boxes.title: Shmuel's View
items: Even just ONE animal in the middle suffices
We view the shepherd as though standing there himself
The verse's 'counter' (moneh) applies to him at that midpoint

summary.principle: Different species and categories — whether produce or animals, whether new-year or old-year — cannot be tithed for one another, and animals join into a single tithing unit only within the physical range a shepherd can actually oversee.

flowSteps.content: 🍇 A fortiori chain: wine/oil don't combine → wine/grain and grain/grain certainly don't → extended even to Rabbi Yoshiya's harder case
🐐 Cattle and flock tithed separately (Abaye: 'the tenth'; Rava: juxtaposition to grain tithe)

columns.content: 🔁 Rava retracts his first position on new/old flocks specifically
🚶 16 mil = shepherd's-eye range; beyond 32 mil, flocks don't combine at all

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Rav needs 5+5+5 to bridge a gap; Shmuel needs only one animal (or even the shepherd himself) in the middle

quiz.q: What is the source for the principle that wine and grain, or grain and a different type of grain, cannot be tithed for each other?
o: It is stated explicitly with no derivation needed
An a fortiori inference from wine and oil, which cannot be tithed together despite not being subject to the diverse-kinds prohibition
It applies only to animals, not produce
Rabbi Akiva invented the rule
quiz.e: The Gemara reasons: if wine and oil, not prohibited as diverse kinds with each other, still cannot be tithed one for the other, then wine and grain (or grain and grain), which ARE subject to diverse-kinds, certainly cannot be tithed together.

quiz.q: According to Abaye, why does the verse 'the tenth shall be sacred to the Lord' prove that cattle and flock must be tithed separately?
o: It doesn't — Abaye disagrees with this rule entirely
It teaches to give the tenth from THIS category and the tenth from THAT category separately
It only applies to sheep and goats
It is derived from Deuteronomy, not Leviticus
quiz.e: Abaye explains that the phrase indicates a separate tenth must be counted and given for the herd and for the flock individually — they cannot be pooled together into one count.

quiz.q: According to the mishna, what is the maximum distance ('the leg of a grazing animal') within which animals join together for tithing purposes?
o: Eight mil
Sixteen mil
Thirty-two mil
There is no maximum
quiz.e: The mishna establishes sixteen mil — the traditional range of a shepherd's watchful eye — as the distance within which animals belonging to one owner combine for animal tithe.

quiz.q: According to Rav, how many animals are needed to bridge two flocks that are thirty-two mil apart?
o: Just one animal in the middle
Five animals on each side plus five in the middle
Ten animals only in the middle
The flocks can never be bridged
quiz.e: Rav requires five animals from each side plus five in the middle — the middle group is 'fit' to combine with either side to reach the necessary total of ten.

quiz.q: According to Shmuel, how many animals in the middle are needed to combine two distant flocks?
o: Ten
Five
Even just one, since we view the shepherd himself as standing at that midpoint
None — Shmuel says distant flocks can never combine
quiz.e: Shmuel holds that even a single animal in the middle suffices, because we regard the shepherd as effectively present there, applying the verse's description of one who 'counts' the flock as a unified group.
